body.name: \mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{loc}}
body.construction: Put \(q=1/4\), \(c_0=1/2\), and \(c_t=c_0+t\kappa_n/q\). Under \(P_t\), conditionally on \(X=x\), let \(D\) and \(Y\) be independent Bernoulli variables. Let the mean of \(D\) be \((1-\kappa_n)/2\) for \(x<c_t\) and \((1+\kappa_n)/2\) for \(x\ge c_t\); let the mean of \(Y\) be \(1/2-q(x-c_0)/2\) for \(x<c_t\) and \(1/2+q(x-c_0)/2\) for \(x\ge c_t\). At \(c_t\), assign response-type masses \(P_t(R=A)=P_t(R=N)=(1-\kappa_n)/2\) and \(P_t(R=C)=\kappa_n\); give always-takers and never-takers common binary potential outcomes with respective means \((1-t\kappa_n)/2\) and \((1+t\kappa_n)/2\), and give compliers potential-outcome means \((1-t)/2\) and \((1+t)/2\). Extend away from \(c_t\) by the same type-independent binary Markov kernel on each observed side that maps the cutoff outcome mean to the declared mean of \(Y\). The resulting continuum is \(\mathcal W_n^{\mathrm{loc}}=\{P_t:t\in[-1,1]\}\).
